_doc: openHC's configuration of the EA3's ADAU1451. See README.md in this directory.
The DSP runs Control4's program, which it boots by itself from the board's
EEPROM (FirmwareVersion cell 0x0dd0 reads 10). That program reads every knob
as an INDEX 0..48 from a parameter cell and looks the setting up in a
49-entry table. Everything in this file is ours: the cell and table
addresses were read off a running unit, and the table CONTENTS are
computed by mkfw.py from the designs below. Nothing here comes from a
A cell's value (an integer) or words (8.24 numbers, or "0x..." raw) are
written at boot; a run value, if it has one, is what
ohc-audiod sets once it is up.
A knob with choices is a selector: the choice's words are written, the
first one at boot. Every other knob is 49 steps with 24 as its neutral,
because that is the size of
the program's tables: tone and EQ steps are step_db apart (0.5 dB gives
Change a design here and rebuild; the web UI shows exactly these knobs.

knobs.label: Mode
knobs._design: the program's output selector, one-hot per channel (left 0x0db5..8, right 0x0db9..c), mapped off a stock unit. Tone shapes with bass and treble, EQ with the ten bands, Flat bypasses both, Test tone plays the program's oscillator. The first choice is the boot one

knobs.label: Loudness
knobs._design: the program's loudness selector, two-way per channel (left 0x0db1..2, right 0x0db3..4)

knobs.label: Bass
knobs._design: the HC-800's tone stage (alsa-ohceq): RBJ shelf, slope 1

knobs.label: Balance
knobs._design: linear, as alsa-ohceq: +100 silences the left channel. Which table is the left output is NOT yet confirmed by ear

cells._doc: 0..Max Volume through the program's volume curve. Written 0 at boot so nothing plays while the box comes up; ohc-audiod sets the run value once it has restored the output's saved level and tone. openHC sets each output's level in ALSA, as on the HC-800, so the DSP runs it full
the program's mute: these words are stock's 'on' (its Master switch writes 0, 0 for off). The program boots it half set, so it is written; silence at boot is Volume's job
which of the program's two volume curves Volume indexes
index into the program's -12..+12 dB gain table at 0x0060
the program's oscillator level, index into its -24..0 dB table at 0x002f; 8 is the program's own value
the program's version cell. No value: never written, and the ReadBack prefix makes the kernel read it fresh every time
